content.title: About
content.content: The Reuben sandwich is a classic American hot sandwich made with rye bread, sauerkraut, corned beef, Swiss cheese, and Russian dressing. It is typically grilled until the bread is golden and the cheese melts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The sandwich was created in the 1920s at Blackstone’s Delicatessen in Omaha, Nebraska.
It is named after the restaurant’s owner, Reuben Kulakofsky.
Traditional recipes use rye bread, though some regions substitute wheat bread.
It is often served with potato chips or pickles on the side.
By the 1940s the Reuben became a staple in U.S. army mess halls.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Corned beef provides high‑quality animal protein essential for tissue repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Red meat contains heme iron, which is readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: Probiotic sauerkraut
items.content: Fermented cabbage supplies beneficial bacteria that support gut health.

items.title: Calcium content
items.content: Swiss cheese adds calcium, important for bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Meat and bread supply B12, B6, and niacin, aiding energy metabolism.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: Sauerkraut and Russian dressing can be salty, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Cheese and beef contain saturated fats that should be limited in heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Swiss cheese may trigger reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk allergy.

items.title: Foodborne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked corned beef can harbor pathogens; it should reach an internal temperature of 63 °C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Place a layer of sauerkraut on a slice of rye bread, add thinly sliced corned beef, top with a slice of Swiss cheese, and drizzle Russian dressing. Grill in a preheated oven at 180 °C for 10‑12 minutes until the cheese melts and the bread is crisp.

content.title: Storage
content.content: The sandwich is best enjoyed fresh. If needed, store it in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Keep cheese and meat wrapped separately at 0‑4 °C to maintain quality.
